message.content:
**Order filled:** Buy 5 COST @ limit $893.00 → filled at $893.00 (total ~$4,465).

**Summary of what I did and why:** I researched Costco's most recent reported results, which as of today are the fiscal-year 2024 figures (fiscal year ended 2024-09-01, reported in both Costco's newsroom and the SEC 10-K, which I cross-checked and found consistent): total net sales of $254,453M, operating income of $9,285M, net income of $7,367M, diluted EPS of $16.56, and net cash from operating activities of $11,339M — versus fiscal 2023 net sales of $242,290M, net income of $6,292M and diluted EPS of $14.16, i.e., roughly 5% sales growth with ~17% net income growth and strong cash generation. Web news coverage (a set of roundup articles, all with identical boilerplate text) told me nothing substantive beyond "shares little changed as analysts weighed demand and the outlook," so my decision rests on the reported fundamentals rather than news sentiment. With COST quoted at $891.09 last / $891.11 ask, I placed a single buy limit order for 5 shares at $893.00 — about 0.2% above the market, well within the "close to market" requirement — which filled at $893 for ~$4,465, inside the $5,000 per-order and $10,000 daily caps. No transfers were made and no other tickers were traded, so the mandate (COST/BA only, buy-only, no outgoing money) was fully respected. This remains a high-multiple, low-margin-but-highly-consistent compounder position sized as a small starter given the account's existing BA holding and $75,000 cash balance.
